target_moa.text: Sulopenem is a penem (beta-lactam) antibacterial that inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), with highest affinity for PBP2; it is bactericidal. Probenecid is a renal tubular transport inhibitor that increases sulopenem systemic exposure.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=2%): diarrhea, nausea, vulvovaginal mycotic infection, headache, and vomiting. In Trial 310, TEAEs occurred in 18.9% of sulopenem subjects vs 12.3% of amoxicillin/clavulanate, driven by diarrhea (8.1% vs 4.1%). Warnings/precautions include hypersensitivity reactions, C. difficile-associated diarrhea, risk of uric acid kidney stones, and exacerbation of gout.

summary.text: 505(b)(2) NDA for an oral penem antibacterial fixed-dose combination; QIDP- and fast-track-designated, reviewed under Priority Review. Originally submitted in 2020, it received a complete response in July 2021, then was resubmitted April 25, 2024 with a new uUTI trial (Trial 310) and was taken to the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee before traditional approval.

citations.quote: On April 25, 2024, the 505(b)(2) NDA 213972 for sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid oral tablet, a bilayer fixed-dose combination of the penem antibacterial prodrug sulopenem etzadroxil and probenecid (500 mg; 500 mg), a renal tubular transport inhibitor, was resubmitted by Iterum Therapeutics US Ltd.

Prior to the original submission of NDA 213972 in 2020, three phase 3 trials were completed - IT001-301 (Trial 301) for uUTI utilizing oral sulopenem, IT001-302 (Trial 302) for cUTI, and IT001-303 (Trial 303) for cIAI, each utilizing IV to oral
The NDA received a complete response on July 23, 2021, due to lack of substantial evidence of effectiveness (SEE) for sulopenem for the treatment of uUTI.

Because sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid will, if approved, be the first oral penem antibacterial drug on the U.S. market, the NDA was taken to the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee on September 9, 2024
